transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Daniel Ruiz (Halo Markets CTO), Anita Gomez (Halo Head of Data), Samir Patel (Halo ML Engineer)

[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro  im ethan from Redwood, and priya our solutions engineer. can everyone say hi?
[00:06] Daniel Ruiz: Hi, Daniel here. thanks for doing this.
[00:09] Anita Gomez: Anita, hi.
[00:11] Samir Patel: Samir  hello.
[00:14] Priya Singh: Great, quick agenda, we want to align on POC goals, what benchmarks to run, integration approach (SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints), and timeline. we'll also touch on security requirements.
[00:27] Anita Gomez: Sounds good. why dont we start with our goals  we want to replace a brittle rule engine that extracts trade events from customer feeds and reduce false positives, and ideally be able to summarize trade threads. accuracy and latency are the main concerns.
[00:42] Daniel Ruiz: And cost  this needs to be economical at scale. our infra team expects predictable costs.
[00:47] Ethan Park: Totally. for the POC we typically define 3 success criteria  accuracy on structured extraction (target > 95% match to golden set), p95 latency under a target, and cost per inference under a threshold. since you mentioned predictability, we can discuss Dedicated pools if needed but we'll start with Hosted to move faster unless you need VPC.
[01:09] Samir Patel: Quick question  typical request is about 1.2k tokens average, some up to 6k. We'll have about 50 RPS at peak in pilot. can Redwood handle that on hosted?
[01:21] Priya Singh: Yes, we can. we want to size the workload more precisely. for 50 RPS with those token sizes we recommend a benchmark slate: 1) latency-only runs at 50 RPS for 30 minutes, 2) cost/throughput run with synthetic bursts, and 3) long tail stability run (6 hours). we'll instrument both token-level metrics and per-route SLOs.
[01:45] Ethan Park: Also important  are you planning any tool/function calling from the model (eg to trigger downstream systems)?
[01:51] Daniel Ruiz: Yes, the model should produce structured JSON that maps to our downstream event schema and ideally call a webhook for downstream processing. we also evaluate model confidence for human-in-the-loop.
[02:01] Priya Singh: Perfect, Redwood supports function/tool-calling patterns and structured output. our OpenAI-compatible endpoint can accept function schemas and return structured output; we also support explicit JSON schema enforcement in our SDK to reduce malformed outputs. we'll include sample schemas in the repo.
[02:19] Samir Patel: Can you talk about the SDK language support and auth? we use python and node primarily.
[02:25] Priya Singh: SDKs for python, node, and go. examples include streaming responses, function calling examples, and structured output validators. auth is API key for hosted, and for Dedicated/Private we support mTLS or cloud IAM plus KMS integrations for secrets.
[02:40] Anita Gomez: On security  SOC2 is a must, we need audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS for key control. data residency is also a question, some EU customers come through our service.
[02:51] Ethan Park: We are SOC2 Type II. we have audit logs per request and can integrate with your KMS (bring-your-own-key) on Dedicated/Private. for Hosted we have region controls; if you need strict EU-only residency we can run the POC in our EU region or plan a Private deployment. i'll send the SOC2 and security pack after this call.
[03:11] Daniel Ruiz: Great. about benchmarks  what's the typical POC timeline and what results will you provide?
[03:17] Priya Singh: We usually run a 4-week POC: week 1 integration + auth + schema alignment, week 2 benchmark runs (latency and throughput), week 3 tuning and repeated runs (quantization or model variant testing), week 4 evaluation + report + business review. deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet with per-route latencies, token-level cost estimates, model recommendations, and a short runbook for production traffic.
[03:40] Samir Patel: For model selection, can we test a smaller quantized variant and a larger higher-accuracy model and compare?
[03:47] Priya Singh: Yes. Redwood catalog lets you pick model variants; our runtime can serve quantized models to save cost. we'll include two variants in the POC and measure accuracy vs cost tradeoffs.
[03:57] Anita Gomez: What about the OpenAI-compatible endpoints  how drop-in is it? our devs already use openai python sdk in parts of our stack.
[04:04] Priya Singh: The endpoints are OpenAI-compatible (same request/response shapes) and we provide SDK adapters and a short migration guide. we also provide example code for function calling and streaming. that should make it nearly drop-in with minimal changes.
[04:16] Ethan Park: One implementation note  if you want strict schema enforcement we recommend using the SDK validator as a pre-check and then also implementing server-side validation before ingestion. that helps avoid schema drift.
[04:28] Daniel Ruiz: Ok, for success criteria let's be explicit:
[04:31] Daniel Ruiz: 1) Structured extraction precision/recall > 95% on our golden set, 2) p95 latency < 400ms at 50 RPS for the typical 1.2k token request, 3) cost per 1M tokens less than $Y (TBD after first benchmark), 4) no PII leakage and auditability with KMS-backed keys.
[04:52] Priya Singh: That all sounds reasonable. we'll add those as the POC success metrics. for the latency target we may need to try both dedicated and hosted variants to see which meets your SLA at the desired cost point.
[05:05] Samir Patel: For the benchmark, what inputs do you need?
[05:08] Priya Singh: 1) 1000 representative requests and labels (golden set), 2) typical long-tail examples (large contexts), 3) expected concurrency profile and peak bursts, 4) a small sample webhook endpoint we can call.
[05:21] Anita Gomez: We can provide that  Samir will upload.
[05:24] Samir Patel: yes i'll upload to the shared drive.
[05:26] Ethan Park: We'll also want a stable test account and temporary API key for the POC. for Dedicated/Private we can provision a temporary sandbox.
[05:34] Daniel Ruiz: How do you measure cost? token counting?
[05:37] Priya Singh: We report token-level metering and per-route breakdown. for the POC we'll provide a cost model: aggregate tokens * model unit cost + infra. it will be in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[05:47] Daniel Ruiz: Any concerns about data retention? We can't keep raw customer messages beyond 30 days in our systems.
[05:54] Ethan Park: We can configure retention policies for logs and request bodies; on Hosted we can do 30-day retention and on Dedicated/Private you control retention. we'll include that option in the security doc.
[06:06] Anita Gomez: About function calling  we expect the model to produce a JSON payload that includes trade_id, timestamp, action_type, and extracted_entities. can Redwood support nested arrays?
[06:16] Priya Singh: Yes, nested JSON is supported. we recommend providing a strict JSON schema; our SDK validator will enforce it and we can return structured outputs or function responses that map exactly to your schema.
[06:28] Daniel Ruiz: What about observability during the POC  tracing, per-route dashboards?
[06:33] Ethan Park: Redwood Console provides route-level latency breakdowns, token-level cost, traces with request IDs, and error analysis. we'll give you a demo instance for the POC and grant access to the Halo team.
[06:44] Samir Patel: Can we run the benchmarks in our VPC or do you run them from Redwood infra?
[06:49] Priya Singh: We can do both. Hosted runs from Redwood infra; for VPC/Private runs we can send a test harness into your network or run the client in your environment hitting the Redwood sandbox. for network-sensitive latency testing VPC is better but more setup.
[07:03] Daniel Ruiz: Timeline  we want results within a month, after that we'll decide on Dedicated if needed.
[07:08] Ethan Park: Understood. we'll propose a 4-week plan and draft an SOW. quick recap and owners at the end.
[07:16] Priya Singh: Recap: deliverables  SDK + sample repo, benchmark spreadsheets, security pack, temporary sandbox credentials, two model variants tested, tuning recommendations.
[07:27] Ethan Park: Next steps: I'll send SOW and pricing, Priya will share SDK and example code, Samir will upload sample data, Daniel will share stakeholder timeline. we'll schedule the benchmark run for week 2  we'll follow up with a calendar invite.
[07:40] Anita Gomez: Thanks everyone.
[07:42] Daniel Ruiz: Thanks. looking forward to it.
[07:44] Ethan Park: thanks all. bye.
